verdicts.reason: A breaks up the three price cards: Yearly and Family sit together, Monthly is stranded alone lower down, and all of them are too small to read. Its CTA is strong and the reading order is otherwise sound. B keeps the three cards together in one row, but in the wrong order (Monthly, Family, Yearly) and still too small. It also puts the legal text above the cards, and the CTA sits off-centre and crowds the left edge.

A's order is a mess: the subtitle and legal text come first and the headline is buried mid-canvas below the cards. The CTA is small and weak, and the Monthly card sits alone at the bottom. B has a sensible flow from logo to headline to CTA, but its price cards are split and too small to read.

A scatters the three cards across the whole canvas, with Monthly jammed against the top edge, Yearly above the headline and Family near the bottom. The logo is demoted to the bottom. B keeps the logo, headline and CTA in a sound hierarchy, though its cards are split and tiny.

A opens with the Family card and the legal text at the very top, and the Yearly card ends up in the bottom-right corner next to the logo. The cards are scattered and the reading order is broken. B's order is coherent, but its cards are fragmented and illegibly small.
